note: the name that starts with what you typed comes first, the one that merely contains it second, and the typo-only one last.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026 on the newest build v26.36.8-d146c39, watched on screen.

Typing ZZPREFIX and opening the Customers tab gives, in this order:
  1. ZZPREFIX Freight Ltd      - the name starts with the word
  2. Bolton ZZPREFIX Services  - the word sits part-way through
  3. ZZPREFIY Cartage          - reachable only by a typo, marked as a close match

The product labels each one as the kind of match it is, and the order follows the requirement. An older warning on this check said it was expected to fail; that was true on the build of 17 September and it does not happen on this one.

note: a made-up word brings back nothing at all, while a real near-spelling still works - so the search is not simply matching anything.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39.

CONTROL FIRST: typing Aabridge - a deliberate near-spelling of a real customer - returns records across eight kinds, including the customer ZZAUTOTEST Aabridge Freight as an exact word match. So near-spelling matching is switched on and working.

THEN THE CHECK: typing Zqwxpol returns nothing anywhere. Every heading reads zero on screen.

That is the point of the check: the search tolerates a misspelling without becoming a machine that answers everything.

note: a name with accents is found whether or not you type the accents.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39.

Typing ZZACC Jose Martinez - no accents - returns the customer ZZACC Jose Martinez, recorded as an exact match on the name.
Typing ZZACC Jose Martinez WITH the accents returns the same single customer, also as an exact match.

Both ways in, one record out, and nothing else returned either time.

note: a name with an apostrophe or a dash is found whether or not you type the punctuation.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39. Four searches, four correct answers:

  ZZPUNC OBrien        -> ZZPUNC O'Brien Haulage      (the only result)
  ZZPUNC O'Brien       -> ZZPUNC O'Brien Haulage      (the only result)
  ZZPUNC Smith Jones   -> ZZPUNC Smith-Jones Motors   (the only result)
  ZZPUNC Smith-Jones   -> ZZPUNC Smith-Jones Motors   (the only result)

Punctuation is treated as optional in both directions, which is what the check asks for.

note: typing a work order number puts that work order on its own line at the very top, above the groups - even though a customer has the same text in its name.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39, read from the screen.

Typing S2-15430 returns two things:
  - the work order S2-15430, shown as a single row ABOVE all the headings, not inside any of them
  - the customer S2-15430 Holdings, inside the Customers heading below it

The work order is recorded as an exact match on its number; the customer is a strong match on its name. The stronger, exact one is lifted out and pinned at the top, which is what this check is for.

note: a part that sits outside the first twenty results is not shown until you narrow the search - and then it appears.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39, read from the screen.

Typing ZZBROAD fills the Parts list with twenty rows and the heading reads twenty. The part we are looking for, ZZBROAD Target Widget, is NOT among them - the list stops at twenty and it ranks below that.

Typing ZZBROAD Target returns exactly one part: ZZBROAD Target Widget. It was always there; it simply was not reachable until the search was made narrower.

That is the behaviour the check asks for: the list caps at twenty with no paging, and narrowing is how a person reaches what is beyond it.

note: a word that only SOUNDS like a part's name does not bring that part back - which is what this check asks for. But read the qualification: the control could not show sound-alike matching working anywhere, so this pass is not proof that the feature exists.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39.

CONTROL FIRST, spelled correctly: typing Knight returns the customer ZZPHON Knight Haulage and the part ZZPHON Knight Bracket, both as exact word matches. So the records are there and reachable.

THE CHECK: typing Nyte - a genuine sound-alike of Knight - returns nothing at all. Typing Nait, a second sound-alike, also returns nothing. The part is not returned, which is what this check requires.

🔴 THE HONEST QUALIFICATION. The requirement says sound-alike matching should work for NAMES but not for parts. On this build neither one comes back: the customer whose name is Knight is not returned by Nyte either. So the control cannot demonstrate that sound-alike matching works at all, and this pass only shows that the part did not leak - not that the feature is behaving as designed.

What needs to be done: the missing sound-alike matching is a question for the Product Owner, not a fault against this check. It is with the QA lead as a decision item. The check itself is not to be rewritten.
